atoms.b: A group of ((five ++ten)) ones is called a <t-blue>ten</t-blue>.
Every number between 1 and 99 is made from <t-blue>tens</t-blue> and ((zeroes ++<t-yellow>ones</t-yellow>)).
The <t-blue>first digit</t-blue> tells you how many ((<t-yellow>ones</t-yellow> ++<t-blue>tens</t-blue>)) are in the number.
The <t-yellow>second digit</t-yellow> tells you how many ((++<t-yellow>ones</t-yellow> <t-blue>tens</t-blue>)) are in the number.
In the number 47 there are ((++4 7 9)) <t-blue>tens</t-blue> and ((4 ++7 9)) <t-yellow>ones</t-yellow>.
